doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Subbing with Will Bradley and Ray McKinley; learning that experience matters
summary: Pete subs for a night with Will Bradley and McKinley, is insulted by McKinley's remark, and reflects on experience and the bands he later played with.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. Before the war, just before the war. And then like I said Carlos Gastel at one time, this was two years after, to me he said, “Hey kid, you want to join the band?” There was somebody by the name of Cohen who was a New York trumpet player, but before that, at Purdue, Will Bradley and Ray McKinley came in for one night to play for a dance and I subbed for one of the trumpet players. He was sick or something. I played the whole © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

night and I remember Ray McKinley, who was a wonderful guy, a great drummer really, and he had the boogie woogie band, you know with Freddie Slack, and I finished the gig and I was really excited. And I overheard Ray McKinley say, “You know when that kid gets some experience he’s going to be great.” Just like that. And I heard and I was insulted. I said what does he mean? I’m going to be great — I said I can do anything Harry does, which I used to do all the technical things Harry did. I says I can imitate Roy Eldridge, and I can play anything. I said what does he mean by that? Well a few years later I knew exactly what he meant. Experience. You can’t explain it, you’ve just got to get it and it will happen, really. It’s something you do and live through. Playing with other musicians, listening to that, being influenced here, everything makes you what you are, or your make-up. You can have all the facilities in the world. I did. I could play anything I wanted. I was very natural. Music, trumpet came very easy for me. And these are the experiences I got when you wind up with the Charlie Barnets and then I played with Basie for a short time, and I did a picture with Duke Ellington’s band, they hired me extra at Paramount for some picture for his band, and they hired me there to play with the band. And it’s wonderful guys, really.
